status_summary: An executive order of 2025-01-23 (Sec. 5) bars executive agencies, unless required by law, from taking action to establish, issue or promote a central bank digital currency in the United States or abroad and directs that any ongoing plans be terminated. Congress completed passage of the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (H.R. 6644) on 2026-06-22 (Senate, 85 to 5) and 2026-06-23 (House, 358 to 32); it was presented on 2026-06-29 and became Public Law 119-101 without the President's signature on 2026-07-11. Its Title XI, Sec. 1101 is summarized by the House Financial Services Committee as prohibiting the Federal Reserve from issuing a CBDC through 2030-12-31, so the statutory bar is time-limited. The House passed the broader H.R. 1919 on 2025-07-17 (219 to 210); no Senate action on it or its companion S. 1124 is recorded.

timeline.event: Executive order on digital financial technology prohibits agencies from establishing, issuing or promoting a CBDC and directs termination of any ongoing CBDC plans (Section 5); it also sets up a working group on digital asset markets.
House passed H.R. 1919, the Anti-CBDC Surveillance State Act, prohibiting Federal Reserve Banks from issuing a CBDC and the Board from testing, studying or developing one (engrossed House text).

GENIUS Act (S. 1582) signed on 2025-07-18 (Public Law 119-27), creating a federal framework for payment stablecoins; the enrolled text on GovInfo does not mention a central bank digital currency, so it neither creates nor bars one.
The Senate concurs in the House amendment to H.R. 6644 (21st Century ROAD to Housing Act) with an amendment (SA 5823), 85 to 5 (Record Vote 182).

The House agrees to the Senate amendment to H.R. 6644, 358 to 32 (Roll no. 224), completing congressional passage of the bill, which includes a time-limited prohibition on the Federal Reserve issuing a CBDC.
H.R. 6644 is presented to the President.

The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (H.R. 6644) becomes Public Law 119-101, dated 2026-07-11 in the law's header. Its table of contents lists Sec. 1101, 'Central bank digital currency,' which the House Financial Services Committee's section-by-section describes as barring the Federal Reserve from issuing a CBDC until the end of 2030 (expiring 2030-12-31). The Duke FinReg Blog reports that it became law without the President's signature and that it covers the Board and Reserve Banks, directly or through intermediaries; The Block places the event on the prior Friday (2026-07-10). The operative text of Sec. 1101 could not be read in the fetched portion. BILLSTATUS records that the bill was sent to the Archivist unsigned, so it became law without the President's signature.
Federal Reserve announced proposals for a GENIUS Act stablecoin issuer framework, open for comment.
